Debauch

/dih-BAWCH/ - the stress falls on BAWCH · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Debauch means to corrupt someone morally by leading them into indulgence.

Tabloids accused the film set of debauching its youngest star, who arrived eager and left unable to keep a call time.

Worked Example

The boy there on a full ride joined the supper club in October. By March his tutors barely saw him: the club's older members kept him out till dawn, paid his tabs, laughed at his deadlines, and treated every warning from the dean as a joke. His grades did not ruin him; his new appetites did.

Debauch is the exact word for what the club did, because it means to corrupt someone morally by leading them into indulgence — the damage is done with pleasures, not threats. Corrupt covers bribes and rigged books; debauch names the slower ruin that arrives dressed as hospitality.

How Debauch Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

corrupt

corrupt: the broad word for bending someone toward wrong — bribes count; debauch works only through indulgence

lead astray

lead astray: the gentle, roomy phrase; debauch is the full ruin

Antonyms

reform

reform: turn someone back toward decent habits

edify

edify: build character up rather than dissolve it

How Strong Is It? — tempt → corrupt → debauch

tempt vs. debauch

tempt vs. debauch: Tempt is a single dangled lure — one dessert, one shortcut — and it can still be refused.

corrupt vs. debauch

corrupt vs. debauch: Corrupt goes further than tempt — the character itself starts to bend; debauch claims the most: a character dissolved wholesale in pleasure, ruin made into a habit.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of debauch.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — de-

Prefix — de-: away

Root — bauch-

Root — bauch-: origin unknown — perhaps an old French word for a workshop's beam

Put it together

Put it together: De- (away) + a puzzle. French débaucher meant to lure a worker away from his duty, and the de- is doing its usual job — away. What bauch- once was is genuinely unknown; one old guess is a workshop's beam, which would make the word literally "to draw someone away from the workbench." The prefix is real; the root kept no other footprint in English.

Why there's no relative to spot

Why there's no relative to spot: Débaucher crossed from French whole, and its second half never lived an English life of its own. You cannot peel debauch down to any root you know — you can only remember where the de- points: away from duty, and downhill from there.

Strength Check

Word Choice

formal / literary, faintly antique

Debauch belongs to court histories and cautionary tales — fortunes, wasted heirs — and it always works through pleasure. Its neighbors divide the labor: corrupt is the plain broad verb and takes bribes as readily as banquets, while this unit's debase lowers a thing's worth rather than a person's morals. If the ruin arrived by envelope, say corrupt; if it arrived by invitation, debauch.
